_source: Statement of Profit and Loss, PDF page 61 of Annual_Report_2024-25Compress_20250910_092510_pdf-2025-Sep-10-09-26-33.pdf (REMC Limited, a joint venture of Indian Railways and RITES Limited -- NOT RITES).
_unit: INR LAKH, exactly as printed. No rescaling. Brackets are negative.
_basis_note: basis is 'unknown': REMC files a single unqualified statement set with no standalone/consolidated anchors, which is what core/basis.py reports and what the FOG keys it under.
_sign_convention: CT is keyed -2681.75 because REMC prints Current Tax IN BRACKETS, as a deduction from PBT. TCS prints the same concept POSITIVE (16,388) with the total tax expense subtracted separately. Keying as-printed is correct for scoring an EXTRACTOR -- it must read what is on the page -- but it means one tag legitimately carries opposite signs across issuers. Normalising that belongs in the reasoning layer, not the truth set.
_oci_out_of_scope: OTCI is deliberately in NEITHER list. REMC discloses the line with an explicit nil ('-'). Whether a disclosed nil should score as 0.0 or as absent is an open design question (see the FOG's nil-row decision), and prejudging it here would bake the answer into the truth set.
_method: Read from the printed statement via `pdftotext -table`, independent of the pipeline's Azure DI OCR. Every subtotal re-derived by hand and ties.
_coverage: FACE LEVEL, deliberately partial. A tag is listed only where its mapping to a printed line is unambiguous. Tags in NEITHER list are out of scope and ignored by score_document -- putting a disclosed-but-unmappable tag in not_reported would score a CORRECT extraction as a false positive.
